compiled_state.title: As the a34c sprint, I want the calibration-channel attribution exercised end-to-end on a real sprint bug before sprint close, so that the program-success question is answerable from day one.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
Self-use validation slice (Probe-1 remediation per sc-7). Creates the tests/fixtures/a34c-sprint-bugs/ fixture with a known detected_by distribution that the correctness tests in the monthly/quarterly story and the closure check below can reference. Adds a Phase-I closure check on this epic that asserts (a) at least one bug filed during the a34c sprint carries a valid detected_by:<channel> tag from the seven allowed values, and (b) calibration-report.sh monthly --fixture=tests/fixtures/a34c-sprint-bugs returns exit 0 with a non-empty bugs-by-channel section that includes the just-filed bug's channel. The closure check runs at Phase I and blocks epic close if either condition fails.

## Done Definitions

- tests/fixtures/a34c-sprint-bugs/ exists with a known detected_by distribution that the monthly/quarterly story's correctness test and the Phase-I closure check both reference ← Satisfies: sc-7
- .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --type=bug returns at least one bug filed during the a34c sprint that carries a detected_by:<channel> tag from the seven allowed values ← Satisfies: sc-7
- calibration-report.sh monthly --fixture=tests/fixtures/a34c-sprint-bugs returns exit 0 with a bugs-by-channel section containing at least one entry, including the just-filed bug's channel ← Satisfies: sc-7
- The Phase-I closure check on this epic asserts both conditions above and blocks epic close if either fails ← Satisfies: sc-7

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The closure check must be runnable by the dso:completion-verifier protocol — emit a typed-enum verdict that check-verifier-verdict.sh recognizes.
- [Self-use] The closure check is itself self-use evidence: if the calibration tooling cannot attribute its own development bugs, the program-success question remains unanswerable. Treat any failure as a blocker, not a warning.

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked
